24 Hours at Black Mountain College

Monday, December 4, 1944 · Lake Eden, Black Mountain, North Carolina · a day in real time

One page per minute: 1,440 pages from midnight to midnight, cut into 315 sequences. When several things happen at once, the film cuts between them; each class keeps a quarter of its own time on screen, so that four classes held at the same hour can all be seen. Between the sequences, nature shots (mountains, sky, stars, frost, trees and wind, birds, animals, insects, sounds of the valley) set the rhythm of the cut: each one shows nature at that very minute and borrows a few seconds from the sequence in progress, so the clock never stops. Colors say what the shot shows: blue, architecture with no one in frame; green, nature (animals and plants); red, collective scenes (teaching, meals, evenings, work); yellow, wide views of nature, buildings, and figures; violet, dialogues; pink, one person reading, writing, or working alone; sequence types take their color from the same palette. Every sequence keeps its sources and its deduced share: ≤ 10% attested by a dated document, 11–40% an attested custom carried over to this day, > 40% assumed, to be confirmed.

Sluglines follow screenplay form (INT./EXT. PLACE — NIGHT, DAWN, DAY, DUSK, from the exact times of dawn, sunrise, sunset, and twilight). “(cont.)” marks a return to a sequence already opened. “(enrolled)” marks students who list the class on their BMC Yearbook record for fall 1944.

Sources: Black Mountain College Community Bulletins and announcements of fall 1944 (Asheville Art Museum, Black Mountain College Collection); Martin Duberman, Black Mountain (1972); David Silver, The Farm at Black Mountain College (2024); Mary Emma Harris interviews; BMC Yearbook (Black Mountain College Museum + Arts Center); weather: NOAA GHCN-Daily and ERA5 reanalysis (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0); sun and moon calculated. Summaries are ours; short quotations only. Working files, in French: github.com/RBMIRC/24hours · the week-by-week calendar: rbmirc.github.io/week.
